title: Athena — Echoes in later ages
summary: Athena, goddess of wisdom and warfare, sprang fully armed from Zeus's head. This study traces the myth's afterlife.
body:
Athena, goddess of wisdom and warfare, sprang fully armed from Zeus's head. She gave Athens the olive tree and became the city's patron.

Long after its gods lost worshippers, Athena kept working — in Renaissance painting, in Romantic poetry, in modern film. Each age found its own anxieties reflected in the old story. Viewed through a contemporary-relevance lens, Athena is brought into the present, where its patterns still appear in new clothes.

Myths survive by being reusable. Athena proved endlessly reusable. A second sub-question concerns the historical kernel: what real events or places might stand behind Athena. Related entries in this archive: Tir na nOg and Odysseus.
key_points: Afterlife of Athena through the centuries.
